vulnerability.title: Guzzle treats a redirect to the same host on a different port as same-origin and forwards Authorization and Cookie headers

affected_packages.note: The 6.x branch was fixed in 6.5.8; the 6.5.8 tag is not present in the local mirror, so that fixed release is recorded from the CNA/NVD/OSV range and was not diffed.

fixed_releases.verified_content: At 7.4.5 RedirectMiddleware uses Psr7\UriComparator::isCrossOrigin() for both header stripping and curl credential removal, and requires psr7 ^1.9 || ^2.4 which provides that comparator

severity.numeric_level_rationale: CNA, NVD Primary, NVD Secondary and GHSA/OSV all publish CVSS 3.1 7.7 High with the same vector; NVD additionally publishes a legacy CVSS 2.0 score of 4.0 Medium, which is a metric-version difference, not a conflict within CVSS 3.1.
severity.source: GitHub_M CNA and nvd@nist.gov (NVD Primary), both CVSS 3.1 7.7 High
severity.ghsa_label_note: GHSA/OSV labels the issue HIGH and publishes the same CVSS 3.1 vector.

vulnerability.category_l2: Redirect handling: the same-origin test compares host and scheme but ignores the port, so credentials survive a redirect to another service on the same host

critical_operation.description: modifyRequest() builds the follow-up request for a redirect and calls shouldStripSensitiveHeaders() to decide whether to drop Authorization and Cookie. That helper returns true on a host difference (line 222) or on an https->http downgrade (line 226); it never calls getPort(), so a redirect from https://host:8443/ to https://host:9443/ is treated as same-origin and the victim's Authorization and Cookie headers are forwarded to whatever service listens on the other port. The same-origin notion is also incomplete on a second, separate site: checkRedirect() unsets curl-managed credentials (CURLOPT_HTTPAUTH/CURLOPT_USERPWD) only when the host differs (line 92), so it misses both scheme and port changes there. The 7.4.5 fix replaces both tests with Psr7\UriComparator::isCrossOrigin(), which compares host, scheme and port (CWE-200).

entry_point.description: A Guzzle client follows a redirect issued by a server to the same host but a different port; the follow-up request carries the original Authorization and Cookie headers.

source_crosscheck.notes: All sources agree on the port-not-compared defect, the 7.x range ending at 7.4.5 and CVSS 3.1 7.7 High. The CNA/NVD affected range also covers the 6.x branch below 6.5.8. The CNA description says the earlier 7.4.2 fix did not cover scheme or port; independently, at 7.4.4 the header-stripping predicate already handled the https->http downgrade, while the curl-managed-credentials path still compared host only, so the fixed commit closes two related but distinct sites. CWE-200 is stated by the CNA and OSV; NVD publishes NVD-CWE-noinfo, i.e. it does not classify rather than contradicting.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read RedirectMiddleware::modifyRequest()/shouldStripSensitiveHeaders() at 7.4.4 and confirm the port is not compared.
An independent reviewer must confirm 1dd98b05 is not an ancestor of 7.4.4 and is the 7.4.5 release containing the UriComparator change.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range and the 7.4.5 fixed release, including the psr7 dependency bump.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.
independent_corrections_accepted: The reviewer supplied the 6.x <6.5.8 range the dossier had omitted; recorded as a second affected range with the verification gap noted.

The reviewer clarified that at 7.4.4 the header path already stripped on https->http, and the scheme gap remained only in the curl-managed-credentials path; the location description now separates the two sites.
The reviewer noted NVD publishes NVD-CWE-noinfo rather than CWE-200; source_crosscheck now records this.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No HTTP client or redirect flow was executed; the leak is established statically from the header-stripping predicate.
Exploitation requires the redirect target on the other port to be controlled by or readable to the attacker, and requires Guzzle redirects to be enabled.
Only the 7.4 branch was diffed; the 6.5.8 fixed release is recorded from the advisory ranges and its tree was not inspected because the mirror lacks that tag.
open_questions: Whether any code path bypasses modifyRequest() when redirects are followed was not exhaustively audited.
How curl-managed credentials interact with the header path in every handler stack was not tested.
